data.name: FlatFatCat
data.detailed_description:
Relax with cats


FlatFatCat is a funny cat billiard game which can help relax, but also offer some challenge. Push "Bruno" our male cat around and try to match different cat pairs. Same colors will fit together and disappear, if you are able to solve the level with just a few shots you can enter a very special game mode. There are hundreds of levels available which offer a variety of different obstacles or objects with special game mechanics. Can you solve all the levels?

This is Bruno, our man character, he is a lazy fat and sometimes a bit crazy male cat.



Bruno wants to bring more fun and joy into his life by getting in contact with other cats. This is not always as easy as it sounds, it takes skill and patience. Sometimes there is a couch or seat in his way, in other rooms are shelves or fish tanks. You need to bounce him, like you would do in a Billiard game, over the floor and throw him in the direction of the other fat cats. If you contact the other cats they will dive over the floor as well. The goal is to resolve all same colored cats by let them bounce together.

How to play


If you match two same colored cats together they will disappear. Your goal is to solve all pairs of cats within the given moves. At the point all cats except Bruno disappeared, the level is cleared – Congratulations! You can reach the Supercat-Mode, when you are able to finish a level with moves left! Stars and points are rewarded according to Combos. Solve over 200 different level in this adventure with many setups and unique objects.

Interactive objects


Bruno’s owner is an ambitious artist. This is why it is possible some buckets of color lay on the floors. It is a big pleasure for Bruno to bounce other cats into this paint.



His wife on the other hand is a florist, and she displays her flowers all over the floor. You can break them!



Bruno dislikes dogs in general, but Chihuahuas are a special treat for him. Their craziness is unpredictable.



He also has to deal with weird looking wheels from time to time. They create an enormous amount of wind, which can be hard to handle.



Some boxes were left after tidying up – the first cat which comes to close will be occupied shredding it for some time…

Conclusion


A crazy cat game with a lot of action ongoing and special Supercat-Mode is available. FlatFatCat is super cute, but it requires some skill to solve all the levels within the given moves. Relax with cats!

reviews.review:
FlatFatCat is a delightful physics-based puzzle game that combines adorable feline characters with billiards-inspired mechanics and increasingly challenging environmental puzzles. Developed and published by Rainware, the game offers a lighthearted experience centered on precision, strategic planning, and creative problem-solving. Its colorful presentation and straightforward concept make it accessible to casual players, while its more demanding stages provide enough complexity to engage dedicated puzzle enthusiasts. Rather than relying on elaborate storytelling or complicated systems, it focuses on transforming simple interactions into entertaining challenges.

The gameplay revolves around Bruno, a remarkably round cat who serves as the primary tool for solving puzzles. Players launch him across different rooms, using collisions to move other cats and bring matching colors together. When two cats of the same color meet, they disappear, bringing the player closer to completing the stage. The objective is to eliminate all matching pairs while keeping Bruno on the playing field. Although this concept sounds simple, the physics-driven movement requires careful consideration of angles, momentum, and positioning, especially when several cats occupy the same environment.

One of the game's strongest features is its emphasis on strategic efficiency. Each level provides a limited number of moves, encouraging players to think carefully before launching Bruno. Randomly striking objects rarely produces consistently successful results, making thoughtful planning essential. Players must anticipate how collisions will influence nearby cats and determine whether a single movement can create multiple successful matches. This introduces a satisfying layer of tactical decision-making that becomes increasingly important as the puzzles grow more complicated.

With more than 200 levels available, FlatFatCat provides a substantial amount of content for its relatively simple premise. The stages feature different room layouts, furniture arrangements, and interactive obstacles that gradually introduce additional considerations. Players encounter increasingly complicated situations that demand more precise movements and creative solutions. The inclusion of scoring opportunities, combination bonuses, and Supercat Mode encourages replaying completed stages to achieve better results. These features provide additional motivation for players interested in mastering the mechanics rather than simply finishing every puzzle.

Environmental interactions add considerable variety to the experience. Paint buckets introduce color-related complications that can influence matching strategies, while cardboard boxes create obstacles capable of temporarily trapping nearby cats. Other objects, including flower arrangements and household furniture, contribute to the playful atmosphere while affecting movement possibilities. Chihuahuas introduce unpredictable interference, and wind-producing devices can alter the movement of objects throughout the environment. These mechanics make the puzzles more dynamic and encourage players to adapt their strategies according to each room's particular arrangement.

The physics system is central to both the game's entertainment value and its difficulty. Watching Bruno bounce between obstacles and send other cats sliding across the floor can produce amusing situations, especially when several interactions occur in quick succession. Successful combinations feel rewarding because they often result from carefully calculated movements. However, the unpredictable nature of multiple collisions can occasionally make precision difficult. Players who prefer completely deterministic puzzle mechanics may find certain situations frustrating, particularly when attempting to complete difficult stages with minimal moves.

Visually, FlatFatCat embraces a cheerful and uncomplicated artistic direction. Its rounded characters, colorful environments, and humorous animations establish a welcoming atmosphere that complements the unusual gameplay concept. The domestic settings give each stage a familiar appearance, while the exaggerated proportions of the cats reinforce the game's playful identity. Although the graphics are relatively modest, their simplicity helps maintain visual clarity during complicated puzzles. The presentation prioritizes personality and accessibility over technical sophistication, making it particularly suitable for players who appreciate charming independent games.

Another advantage is its flexibility for different playing habits. Individual stages are generally suitable for short gaming sessions, allowing players to complete a few puzzles without making a substantial time commitment. Meanwhile, the extensive level selection and opportunities for improved scores provide additional engagement for completionists. Steam achievements further encourage progression and experimentation. Nevertheless, the repetitive nature of launching cats and matching colors may eventually become noticeable, especially for players seeking frequent changes in gameplay mechanics or a more substantial narrative experience.

Regarding technical accessibility, the game has modest system requirements, including 512 MB of RAM, OpenGL 2.0 graphics support, and approximately 90 MB of storage space. Its lightweight design makes it approachable for players using less powerful computers. The availability of Windows, macOS, and SteamOS/Linux support also broadens its potential audience. These specifications suggest that the experience does not depend on demanding hardware, although actual performance remains dependent on individual system configurations.

Steam Deck compatibility remains officially unverified, with no confirmed Verified or Playable classification established for the game. Its SteamOS/Linux support and minimal hardware requirements suggest that running it on Valve's handheld may be possible. However, controller functionality and input configuration could require adjustments, particularly if certain interactions depend on mouse controls. The game's compact stages and relatively simple mechanics make it conceptually well suited to portable gaming, but full compatibility should not be assumed without additional testing.

Despite its appealing design, FlatFatCat is not without limitations. Its central gameplay loop remains largely unchanged throughout the experience, and some players may eventually find the matching mechanics repetitive. The limited-move system can also create frustration when complicated physics interactions prevent otherwise reasonable solutions. Nevertheless, these shortcomings are balanced by the substantial number of levels, entertaining environmental elements, and satisfying opportunities for strategic experimentation.

Overall, FlatFatCat delivers an enjoyable combination of casual puzzle-solving, humorous animal interactions, and physics-based challenges. Its accessible controls, charming presentation, and generous level selection make it an appealing option for players seeking an uncomplicated yet occasionally demanding experience. While it does not dramatically reinvent the puzzle genre, its creative use of collisions and environmental obstacles gives it a distinctive personality.

A charming and entertaining physics puzzler that offers considerable content, satisfying challenges, and playful creativity, although occasional repetition and unpredictable collisions prevent it from achieving its full potential.

Rating: 6/10
